introduction_markdown:
**Time allowed: three hours.** Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. Verify that this booklet contains six questions, no questions are repeated and there are no blank pages. Inform the invigilator in case this booklet contains less than six questions, questions are repeated or there are blank pages so that the booklet should be changed. Blank spaces in this question booklet may be used for rough work. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Calculators may be used.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses (RAM): C = 12.0, O = 16.0, H = 1.0, Na = 23.0.

The paper has three sections: Section A - Physical and General Chemistry (questions 1 and 2); Section B - Inorganic Chemistry (questions 3 and 4); Section C - Organic Chemistry (questions 5 and 6).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the reaction scheme below and answer the questions that follow.

![fig-1](gce-al-chemistry-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(The scheme: A ($\mathrm{C_3H_6}$) reacts by step w to give B ($\mathrm{C_3H_7Br}$); B reacts by step x to give C ($\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$); C reacts by step y to give D ($\mathrm{C_3H_6O_2}$); C also reacts by step z to give $\mathrm{C_3H_6}$ (A); A with $\mathrm{O_3}$ then Zn dust gives $\mathrm{CH_2O}$ (E) + F.)

(i) Write down the structural formulae of compounds A, B, C, D and F.

A:    B:    C:    D:    F:

(ii) Suggest the reagent(s) and reaction condition(s) for the reactions w, x, y and z.

| | Reagent(s) | Reaction condition(s) |
|---|---|---|
| w | | |
| x | | |
| y | | |
| z | | |

*[9 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Structural formulae.**

- **A**, $\mathrm{C_3H_6}$, is **propene**, $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2}$ (it is regenerated from C in step z, and ozonolysis gives methanal + F).
- **F** is the other ozonolysis product: $\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2 \xrightarrow{O_3,\,Zn} HCHO + CH_3CHO}$, so **F = ethanal, $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$** (E is methanal, $\mathrm{HCHO}$, i.e. $\mathrm{CH_2O}$).
- **B**, $\mathrm{C_3H_7Br}$: **1-bromopropane, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Br}$**.
- **C**, $\mathrm{C_3H_8O}$: **propan-1-ol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}$**.
- **D**, $\mathrm{C_3H_6O_2}$: **propanoic acid, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$**.

Reasoning: D has two oxygens, so it is a carboxylic acid formed by oxidising a **primary alcohol** (a secondary alcohol such as propan-2-ol would give propanone, $\mathrm{C_3H_6O}$). So C is propan-1-ol and B is 1-bromopropane, which means that in step w, HBr adds to propene in the **anti-Markovnikov** sense.

**(ii) Reagents and conditions.**

| Step | Reagent(s) | Reaction condition(s) |
|---|---|---|
| w | HBr (hydrogen bromide) | In the presence of a **peroxide** (e.g. $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ or benzoyl peroxide), non-polar solvent: free-radical addition giving 1-bromopropane (without peroxide the product is 2-bromopropane) |
| x | Aqueous sodium (or potassium) hydroxide, NaOH(aq) | Heat under reflux (nucleophilic substitution) |
| y | Acidified potassium dichromate(VI), $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7/H_2SO_4}$ (or acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$) | Heat under **reflux** with excess oxidising agent (so the aldehyde is oxidised on to the acid) |
| z | Concentrated sulphuric acid, conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (or $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$) | Heat to about $170^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ with excess acid (dehydration, elimination of water); or pass the alcohol vapour over hot $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ at about $350^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ |

questions.enonce_markdown:
How can you distinguish by a chemical test the following pairs of compounds?

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_2CH_3}$

(ii) $\mathrm{C_2H_5COOH}$ and $\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}OH}$

(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ and $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3N}$ *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Pentan-3-one, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3}$, and pentan-2-one, $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_2CH_3}$ - the iodoform (tri-iodomethane) test.** Warm each compound with aqueous iodine and sodium hydroxide ($\mathrm{I_2/NaOH(aq)}$). **Pentan-2-one**, which contains the $\mathrm{CH_3CO{-}}$ group, gives a **pale yellow precipitate of iodoform, $\mathrm{CHI_3}$**, with an antiseptic smell; **pentan-3-one** gives no yellow precipitate.

**(ii) Propanoic acid and phenol.** Add a solution of **sodium hydrogencarbonate** (or sodium carbonate) to each. **Propanoic acid** gives **effervescence of carbon dioxide** (it turns lime water milky); **phenol** is too weak an acid to react, so there is no gas. Confirmation: add neutral **iron(III) chloride** solution: phenol gives a **violet (purple) colour**, propanoic acid does not.

**(iii) Ethylamine (primary amine) and trimethylamine (tertiary amine).** Add **nitrous acid** (sodium nitrite and dilute hydrochloric acid, kept below $5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$). The **primary aliphatic amine** gives **bubbles of nitrogen gas** (effervescence) with formation of an alcohol; the **tertiary amine** gives **no gas** (it only forms a soluble salt). (Alternative: warm with chloroform and ethanolic KOH, the carbylamine test: the primary amine alone gives a foul-smelling isocyanide.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carbon undergoes $\mathrm{sp^3}$, $\mathrm{sp^2}$ and $\mathrm{sp}$ hybridisations in order to bond to itself and with other elements.

(i) What is hybridisation?

(ii) On the structure of vitamin C (ascorbic acid) below circle any three $\mathrm{sp^3}$ carbon atoms and then place an asterisk on all the $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridised carbon atoms.

![fig-1](gce-al-chemistry-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

(Structure as printed: a five-membered ring containing a ring oxygen, with a C=O (lactone) carbon, a C=C double bond bearing two OH groups, and a ring carbon carrying the side chain $\mathrm{CH(OH)CH_2OH}$.) *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Hybridisation** is the **mixing (combination) of atomic orbitals of different types and similar energy (an s orbital with one, two or three p orbitals) on the same atom to form an equal number of new, equivalent hybrid orbitals** of the same energy and shape, which then overlap with other orbitals to form covalent bonds (sp$^3$: four hybrid orbitals, tetrahedral, $109.5^{\circ}$; sp$^2$: three, trigonal planar, $120^{\circ}$; sp: two, linear, $180^{\circ}$).

**(ii) Vitamin C** has six carbon atoms, three sp$^2$ and three sp$^3$:

- **sp$^2$ carbons (mark each with an asterisk, *):** the **lactone carbonyl carbon** (C=O in the ring) and the **two carbons of the C=C double bond** (each carrying an OH). Each has a double bond and three $\sigma$ bonds (trigonal planar).
- **sp$^3$ carbons (circle these; there are exactly three):** the **ring carbon bonded to the ring oxygen and to the side chain** (the CH of the ring), the **$\mathrm{CH(OH)}$ carbon** of the side chain and the **$\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ carbon**. Each carbon has four single ($\sigma$) bonds (tetrahedral).

No carbon in ascorbic acid is sp hybridised (there is no triple bond or $\mathrm{C{=}C{=}C}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Suggest the spectroscopic methods that could be used to identify the following:

(i) Positions of hydrogen atom.

(ii) Presence of double bonds. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Positions of hydrogen atoms:** **proton ($^1\mathrm{H}$) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy**: the chemical shifts, the integration (number of H in each environment) and the splitting pattern show where the hydrogen atoms are in the molecule.

**(ii) Presence of double bonds:** **infrared (IR) spectroscopy**: a $\mathrm{C{=}C}$ stretch absorbs at about $1620$-$1680\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ and a $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ stretch at about $1680$-$1750\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$. (Ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy also detects conjugated double bonds.)
